Assume \(K>0\) (in particular, \(K\) may be a positive integer). Define

\[
\psi(\lambda)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Phi(\lambda x)^K\phi(x)\,dx .
\]

### 1. Symmetry
Using the substitution \(x\mapsto -x\),

\[
\psi(-\lambda)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Phi(-\lambda x)^K\phi(x)\,dx
=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\Phi(\lambda x)^K\phi(x)\,dx
=\psi(\lambda).
\]

So \(\psi\) is an even function; its behavior is determined by \(\lambda>0\).

### 2. Derivative
Differentiating under the integral sign,

\[
\psi'(\lambda)
=K\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} x\,\phi(x)\,\phi(\lambda x)\,\Phi(\lambda x)^{K-1}\,dx .
\]

For \(\lambda>0\), pair the contributions from \(x\) and \(-x\):

\[
\psi'(\lambda)
=
K\int_0^\infty
x\,\phi(x)\,\phi(\lambda x)
\left[
\Phi(\lambda x)^{K-1}-\Phi(-\lambda x)^{K-1}
\right]dx .
\]

For \(x>0\),

\[
0<\Phi(-\lambda x)<\frac12<\Phi(\lambda x)<1.
\]

Hence:

- If \(K>1\), then \(t^{K-1}\) is increasing on \((0,1)\), so the bracket is positive. Thus \(\psi'(\lambda)>0\) for \(\lambda>0\).
- If \(K=1\), the bracket is zero, so \(\psi'(\lambda)=0\).
- If \(0<K<1\), then \(t^{K-1}\) is decreasing on \((0,1)\), so the bracket is negative. Thus \(\psi'(\lambda)<0\) for \(\lambda>0\).

Therefore, for \(K>1\), \(\psi(\lambda)\) strictly increases with \(|\lambda|\); for \(0<K<1\), it strictly decreases with \(|\lambda|\).

### 3. Endpoint values
At \(\lambda=0\),

\[
\psi(0)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac12\right)^K\phi(x)\,dx
=2^{-K}.
\]

As \(|\lambda|\to\infty\), \(\Phi(\lambda x)^K\to \mathbf 1_{x>0}\) for \(\lambda\to+\infty\), and \(\to \mathbf 1_{x<0}\) for \(\lambda\to-\infty\). In both cases,

\[
\lim_{|\lambda|\to\infty}\psi(\lambda)
=
\int_0^\infty \phi(x)\,dx
=
\frac12.
\]

### 4. Extrema

- If \(K>1\), then \(2^{-K}<\frac12\). Since \(\psi\) increases with \(|\lambda|\) to the limit \(\frac12\), the unique global minimum occurs at \(\lambda=0\). There is no finite maximizing \(\lambda\); the supremum is \(\frac12\), approached as \(|\lambda|\to\infty\).

- If \(K=1\), then \(\psi(\lambda)\equiv \frac12\) for all \(\lambda\).

- If \(0<K<1\), then \(2^{-K}>\frac12\). Since \(\psi\) decreases with \(|\lambda|\) to the limit \(\frac12\), the unique global maximum occurs at \(\lambda=0\). There is no finite minimizing \(\lambda\); the infimum is \(\frac12\), approached as \(|\lambda|\to\infty\).

Thus, in the usual case where \(K\) is an integer greater than \(1\), the expression is minimized at \(\lambda=0\), and it has no finite maximum.

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
K>1: & \lambda=0 \text{ gives the unique global minimum; no finite maximum, } \sup_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)=\frac12,\\[4pt]
K=1: & \psi(\lambda)=\frac12 \text{ for all } \lambda,\\[4pt]
0<K<1: & \lambda=0 \text{ gives the unique global maximum; no finite minimum, } \inf_{\lambda}\psi(\lambda)=\frac12.
\end{cases}
}
\]
